worst.problem: When the script cap is hit, the engine and the brief rules let the agent say a flag provider is absent, even though only 2% of scripts were read. Provider detection also misses gate call sites such as checkGate, useGate and getFeatureGate, so even scripts that were read can fail to count as a provider. This causes the blocking false-absence stumble on notion-marketplace, and the eval's must_state 'checkGate' cannot pass.
worst.fix: 1) Add call-signature fingerprints (`checkGate(`, `useGate(`, `getFeatureGate(`, `getExperiment(`) to statsig-sdk.json so any script that was read registers the provider. 2) In emit.py, when cap_hit and no provider was found, print a coverage line: 'runtime flag provider: none found in the N of M scripts read (capped)'. 3) Add one sentence to brief.md: an absence under a cap is written as 'not found in the N scripts read', never as 'not detected'.
worst.expected_effect: The blocking notion-marketplace stumble ('No runtime flag provider was detected') goes away. The brief stops stating unsupported absences, and the notion-marketplace eval is more likely to pass its must_state 'checkGate' check whenever a gate call site is among the scripts read.

fixer: Any read script that calls checkGate(, useGate(, getFeatureGate( or getExperiment( now registers Statsig as a provider; when the cap is hit and no provider is found, the coverage block prints 'runtime flag provider: none found in the N of M scripts read (capped)'; and brief.md now says an absence under a cap is written as 'not found in the N scripts read', never as 'not detected'.
